newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil shoots up on stronger IPE.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil shoots up on stronger IPE.

text.p: Singapore gas oil firmed as prices on the London-based International Petroleum Exchange shot up to a five-year high.
Traders said structurally, gas oil in Singapore for September lifting was tight as there were reduced exports of gas oil from the MidEast to this region.
MidEast producers chose to sell their product to the more lucrative markets in the Mediterrean and East Africa.
Traders were bidding at up to $27.20 with no seller emerging. Jet fell slightly with offers seen at $29.20 on talks of high stocks in Guam, Singapore and the MidEast.
Gasoline remained bearish with bids/offers talked lower $21.50/$22.50 per barrel for early October liftings of 50,000 barrels of 95-octane of unleaded gasoline, compared to Thursday's deal at $22.50.

A Thai refiner said it's next availability would be in October after having already sold its early September lifting cargo of 250,000 barrels of 95-octane at close to 25 cents per barrel below Singapore quotes fob Sri Racha.
Naphtha firmed in line with higher crude and Singapore swaps values. September swaps rose slightly to $20.35-$20.60, up 10 cents from Thursday's close.

Fuel oil was slightly firmer with a buyer heard at $113 a tonne for October 1-5 lifting. Although stocks are low in Singapore, firm prices are expected to attract more cargoes in late September. Weak Chinese demand has also prompted some South Korean sellers to show cargoes in Singapore, traders said.

The LSWR market remained in the doldrums with slack demand, which has backed up liftings at Platinum, Indonesia's floating storage. India's demand was already covered by a Japanese trader who sold 200,000 barrels at $3.50 a barrel over Pertamina's formula, c-and-f Bombay for second half September delivery.
